Goal:
Create a Python implementation that is a 1:1 functional port of the reference application for this benchmark. For the same input, the official reference CLI and your rebuilt version must produce exactly the same observable result: exit status, stdout, and stderr.

Reference:
- Project: xsv
- Source language: Rust
- Target language: Python
- Repository: https://github.com/BurntSushi/xsv.git
- Release/tag: 0.13.0

- Local source copy: ./rust-reference
- Official reference CLI: read ./REFERENCE_BINARY.txt
- Behavior area: headers, count, select, slice, search, sort, table, fmt, stats, frequency

Hard constraints:
- Do not use Docker.
- Do not search the internet.
- Do not look for, copy, adapt, vendor, install, or import an existing Python implementation, clone, wrapper, compatibility layer, or package for this application.
- Use ./rust-reference and the official reference CLI as the only functional sources of truth.
- Implement in Python.
- Do not shell out to the official reference CLI from your implementation.
- Do not install packages that already implement this application or its command suite.
- The root deliverable must include ./compile.sh.
- ./compile.sh must build or wrap your Python implementation and leave a runnable root command named ./executable. On Windows, ./executable.exe or ./executable.cmd is also accepted.
- The first entrypoint discovered by the evaluator must itself be directly runnable on the current OS/runtime; do not leave a higher-priority wrapper, placeholder, or script that requires a different interpreter than the evaluator will use.
- The harness will run ./compile.sh and then invoke your runnable executable with the same argv used for the official reference CLI.

Deliverable shape:
- Keep the actual implementation in one or more Python files, for example ./main.py or ./xsv_port.py.
- ./compile.sh must be idempotent and must create only entrypoints that are directly runnable by the evaluator on this machine.
- The evaluator checks entrypoints in this order: ./executable, ./executable.exe, ./executable.cmd, ./executable.bat, ./executable.js, ./executable.py, ./executable.jar.
- For a Python target, if ./executable exists, it must be valid Python source that can be run as: python ./executable <args>. Do not make ./executable a POSIX shell script.

- If the official binary writes to stderr, your program must write to stderr.

Do not ask the user questions. Infer from source and official CLI behavior.

+import csv
+import os
+import random
+import shutil
+import string
+import subprocess
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
+REF = Path((ROOT / "REFERENCE_BINARY.txt").read_text().strip())
+PORT = [sys.executable, str(ROOT / "executable")]
+WORK = ROOT / ".tura" / "verify_cases"
+
+
+def run(cmd, stdin=b"", cwd=None):
+    p = subprocess.run(cmd, input=stdin, cwd=cwd or ROOT, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
+    return p.returncode, p.stdout, p.stderr
+
+
+def write_csv(path, rows, delimiter=","):
+    with path.open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
+        w = csv.writer(f, delimiter=delimiter, lineterminator="\n")
+        w.writerows(rows)
+
+
+def cell(rng):
+    choices = ["", "a", "b", "x y", "1", "-2", "3.5", "001", "NULL", "quote\"q", "comma,value", " z "]
+    if rng.random() < 0.25:
+        return "".join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-") for _ in range(rng.randrange(0, 12)))
+    return rng.choice(choices)
+
+
+def table(rng, rows=None, cols=None, headers=True):
+    cols = cols or rng.randrange(1, 6)
+    n = rows if rows is not None else rng.randrange(0, 12)
+    head = ["h{}".format(i + 1) for i in range(cols)]
+    if cols >= 2 and rng.random() < 0.25:
+        head[-1] = head[0]
+    body = [[cell(rng) for _ in range(cols)] for _ in range(n)]
+    return ([head] if headers else []) + body
+
+
+def valid_select(rng, cols, use_names=True):
+    forms = ["", "1", "1-", "-{}".format(cols), "1-{}".format(cols), "!1", "1,1"]
+    if cols >= 2:
+        forms += ["2", "{}-1".format(cols), "1,{}".format(cols)]
+    if use_names:
+        forms += ["h1", "h1[0]", "h1-h{}".format(cols), '"h1"']
+    return rng.choice(forms)
+
+
+def invalid_select(rng, cols, use_names=True):
+    forms = ["0", str(cols + rng.randrange(1, 4)), '"h1', "h1[abc]", "a-b-"]
+    if use_names:
+        forms.append("missing")
+    else:
+        forms.append("h1")
+    return rng.choice(forms)
+
+
+def make_case_dir(name):
+    d = WORK / name
+    shutil.rmtree(d, ignore_errors=True)
+    d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    return d
+
+
+def cases_for(cmd, rng, valid, count):
+    for i in range(count):
+        d = make_case_dir(f"{cmd}_{'v' if valid else 'i'}_{i}")
+        cols = rng.randrange(1, 6)
+        rows = table(rng, cols=cols, headers=True)
+        path = d / "in.csv"
+        write_csv(path, rows)
+        base = [cmd]
+        if cmd == "headers":
+            if valid:
+                opts = rng.choice([[], ["--just-names"], ["--intersect"]])
+                yield opts + [str(path)], b"", d
+            else:
+                yield ["--delimiter", "xx", str(path)], b"", d
+        elif cmd == "count":
+            yield ((["--no-headers"] if valid and rng.random() < 0.5 else []) + ([str(path)] if valid else ["--delimiter", "xx", str(path)])), b"", d
+        elif cmd == "select":
+            sel = valid_select(rng, cols, True) if valid else invalid_select(rng, cols, True)
+            yield [sel, str(path)], b"", d
+        elif cmd == "slice":
+            if valid:
+                opts = rng.choice([[], ["--start", str(rng.randrange(0, 5))], ["--end", str(rng.randrange(0, 8))], ["--len", str(rng.randrange(0, 5))], ["--index", str(rng.randrange(0, 5))]])
+            else:
+                opts = rng.choice([["--index", "1", "--start", "0"], ["--end", "1", "--len", "1"], ["--start", "5", "--end", "2"]])
+            yield opts + [str(path)], b"", d
+        elif cmd == "search":
+            if valid:
+                opts = rng.choice([[], ["--ignore-case"], ["--invert-match"], ["--select", valid_select(rng, cols, True)]])
+                yield opts + [rng.choice(["a", "^1", "z", ".*", "[0-9]"]), str(path)], b"", d
+            else:
+                yield [rng.choice(["[", "("],), str(path)], b"", d
+        elif cmd == "sort":
+            if valid:
+                opts = rng.choice([[], ["--numeric"], ["--reverse"], ["--select", valid_select(rng, cols, True)]])
+            else:
+                opts = ["--select", invalid_select(rng, cols, True)]
+            yield opts + [str(path)], b"", d
+        elif cmd == "table":
+            if valid:
+                opts = rng.choice([[], ["--width", str(rng.randrange(1, 6))], ["--pad", str(rng.randrange(1, 5))], ["--condense", str(rng.randrange(1, 6))]])
+            else:
+                opts = [["--width", "bad"], ["--delimiter", "xx"]][i % 2]
+            yield opts + [str(path)], b"", d
+        elif cmd == "fmt":
+            if valid:
+                opts = rng.choice([[], ["--out-delimiter", "\t"], ["--crlf"], ["--ascii"], ["--quote-always"], ["--escape", "\\"]])
+            else:
+                opts = rng.choice([["--quote", "xx"], ["--delimiter", "xx"]])
+            yield opts + [str(path)], b"", d
+        elif cmd == "stats":
+            if valid:
+                opts = rng.choice([[], ["--median"], ["--mode"], ["--cardinality"], ["--everything"], ["--select", valid_select(rng, cols, True)], ["--nulls"]])
+            else:
+                opts = ["--select", invalid_select(rng, cols, True)]
+            yield opts + [str(path)], b"", d
+        elif cmd == "frequency":
+            if valid:
+                opts = rng.choice([[], ["--limit", str(rng.randrange(0, 5))], ["--asc"], ["--select", valid_select(rng, cols, True)], ["--no-nulls"]])
+            else:
+                opts = ["--select", invalid_select(rng, cols, True)]
+            yield opts + [str(path)], b"", d
+
+
+def main():
+    seed = os.environ.get("VERIFIER_SEED", str(random.randrange(1 << 30)))
+    rng = random.Random(seed)
+    print("seed", seed)
+    commands = ["headers", "count", "select", "slice", "search", "sort", "table", "fmt", "stats", "frequency"]
+    total = 0
+    for cmd in commands:
+        for valid, n in [(True, 16), (False, 4)]:
+            for args, stdin, cwd in cases_for(cmd, rng, valid, n):
+                total += 1
+                ref = run([str(REF), cmd] + args, stdin, cwd)
+                got = run(PORT + [cmd] + args, stdin, cwd)
+                if ref != got:
+                    print("FAIL", cmd, "valid" if valid else "invalid", args)
+                    print("REF", ref[0], ref[1].decode('utf-8','replace'), ref[2].decode('utf-8','replace'))
+                    print("GOT", got[0], got[1].decode('utf-8','replace'), got[2].decode('utf-8','replace'))
+                    return 1
+    print("ok", total)
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())
*** End Patch
